notes: To desire strongly, to long for someone. In 1:8, Paul yearns for the Philippians "with the affection of Christ Jesus." The noun epipothēsis appears in 2 Corinthians 7.

Longing to be clothed with our habitation.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: That your love may abound yet more and more in knowledge and all discernment.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: Through the law comes the knowledge of sin.
Until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God.
Increasing in the knowledge of God.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: I also practice always having a conscience void of offense toward God and men.
Give no occasion for stumbling.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

elsewhere.note: I stir up your sincere mind by reminder.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

Whom I have begotten in my bonds.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

My defense to those who examine me.
Always being ready to give a defense.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

Making himself equal with God.

elsewhere.note: He didn't consider equality with God a thing to be grasped.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.

That our boasting may not be in vain.

Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord.

review.note: Hand-written first draft from general knowledge. Check against commentaries and a lexicon.
